proposed_comments.body: The comment says erasing stops on click again “(or releases)”, but the implementation is click-to-toggle only: WM_LBUTTONUP returns early and does not disengage the eraser. This makes the comment misleading for future maintainers.

Shift+E can currently toggle the eraser while a pen stroke is in progress (g_Tracing==TRUE). That leaves WM_LBUTTONUP short-circuited by the eraser check (so g_Tracing never resets) and can put the drawing state machine into an inconsistent state. Consider disallowing Shift+E while tracing.

In the WM_MOUSEMOVE tracing path, erasing happens whenever g_EraserMode!=Off, even if the eraser hasn’t been engaged (g_EraserEngaged==FALSE). This bypasses the intended click-to-toggle model and can cause unexpected erasing if the mode is toggled while tracing.

The eraser mode popup uses hardcoded English strings ("Eraser: Pixel/Stroke/Off"), which are user-facing but not localizable. Consider moving these labels to resources (e.g., string table in ZoomIt.rc + LoadStringW) so they can be translated consistently with other UI text.

EraseConnectedStroke allocates two full-screen 32bpp DIBSections and does full-screen BitBlt/BlankScreenArea on every call. In stroke mode this can run repeatedly during mouse move, leading to very large allocations (width*height*8 bytes plus visited/stack) and severe UI jank or OOM on high-resolution displays. Consider reusing cached bitmaps/DCs across calls (recreate only on size change) and/or restricting the flood-fill snapshot to a bounded region.

IDC_ERASER is introduced with the same numeric value as IDC_WEBCAM_BACKGROUND_BLUR (1124). Reusing IDs across unrelated controls can make WM_COMMAND-style routing and future maintenance error-prone; it’s safer to assign a new unique value for the new control.

This new file appears to be an auto-generated MIDLRT output from PowerRenameXAML\\App.idl and is unrelated to the ZoomIt eraser feature. Generated headers are typically produced under $(GeneratedFilesDir) during build and shouldn’t be checked into source control; please remove it from the PR (and ensure the build output path is ignored).

confidence.rationale: The exact extracted production dispatch reproduces the upstream destructive fallthrough and proves the literal early exit changes only layered Shift+E while preserving plain E, the non-layered cycle, and typing mode; the candidate also compiles and links on the pinned head.

proposed_comments.title: Resize the options host for the expanded Draw page
proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: The complete correction must enlarge the unchanged OPTIONS dialog and IDC_TAB host in src/modules/ZoomIt/ZoomIt/ZoomIt.rc; the PR only changes the Draw page, so no current RIGHT-side range can contain the full fix.
proposed_comments.body:
### Resize the options host for the expanded Draw page

**Severity:** `high`

**Affected code:** `src/modules/ZoomIt/ZoomIt/ZoomIt.rc` (`OPTIONS` and `DRAW` dialog templates) and `src/modules/ZoomIt/ZoomIt/Zoomit.cpp` (`OptionsAddTabs` and `RepositionTabPages`).

**Problem:** This PR extends the Draw page to 249 dialog units and places its last controls through y=243, but the unchanged multiline `IDC_TAB` host remains 255 units tall. `OptionsAddTabs` and `RepositionTabPages` call `TabCtrl_AdjustRect` and then force every child page to that smaller display rectangle, so the tab headers and borders reduce the available page height below the new Draw content and clip the Screen/help/hotkey controls.

**Why it matters:** The new eraser help consumes the remaining vertical space and can leave existing Draw settings hidden or cut off instead of making the expanded page usable.

**Suggested change:**
1. Increase `OPTIONS` from 299x331 to 299x373 and move OK/Cancel, Show tray icon, and Run ZoomIt when Windows starts down by 42 units.
2. Increase `IDC_TAB` from height 255 to 297 so the display rectangle produced by `TabCtrl_AdjustRect` grows with the host.
3. Increase `DRAW` from height 249 to 270; move the Screen heading/help text and Draw without Zoom hotkey/label down by 20 units to retain spacing below the new eraser section.
4. Keep the existing `OptionsAddTabs`/`RepositionTabPages` sizing path; no special-case page positioning is needed once the resource geometry is internally consistent.

**Verification:** Build ZoomIt, then open Options > Draw at 100%, 150%, and 200% scaling in light and dark themes. Confirm the eraser text, Screen section, and Draw without Zoom hotkey are fully visible, the bottom dialog controls remain reachable, and switching tabs or changing DPI keeps each page inside the tab display rectangle.

confidence.rationale: The pinned resource geometry exceeds the display area to which production tab-host code resizes every page. The complete resource-only correction compiled and linked alone and together with the inline fix; visual DPI/theme checks remain author-facing verification.
